function: PPO jointly learns RIS phase shifts and transmit power (physical layer) with task offloading and CPU frequency; GLAA path selection is non-learned (pp. 1, 11).
system: 100 single-antenna IoT devices, 10 ECNs with Q antennas (value not given), 20 passive RISs of 32 elements, 10 MHz bandwidth; carrier not stated (pp. 6, 12).
method: Modified PPO (adaptive KL-based clipping), actor-critic with two 512-neuron hidden layers, reinforcement learning on an energy-latency overhead reward; LLM-based IAI guides the agent (pp. 6, 11-12).
data_channel: Own simulator: random user and ECN coordinates, log-normal path loss with shadowing for signal strength, simulated patient vitals; channel gain distributions not specified; no dataset (pp. 7, 12).
test_conditions: Training and evaluation in the same simulator; sweeps over number of IoT nodes, ECNs and users; no unseen scenario or held-out condition is stated (pp. 13-16).
baselines: Manual modeling (MM) with standard or modified PPO; standard PPO; static model with fixed RIS phases and routing; non-RIS; greedy algorithm for execution time (pp. 13-16).
metrics: Cumulative energy-latency overhead, total reward, latency, throughput, energy efficiency, efficiency score, execution time (pp. 13-16).
complexity: Order of complexity of standard and modified PPO networks in Table II (p. 11); execution time of GA versus GLAA in Fig. 9c (p. 14).
q1_support: p. 7: "calculated based on the Log-normal path loss model". The channel vectors h, H and g (p. 6) have no stated distribution and coordinates are random (p. 12); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 14: "the impact of increasing the number of IoT nodes and ECNs on latency". These are sweeps of the network size (Figs. 8-11); the paper does not state that an agent trained in one setting was tested in another.
q3_support: p. 13: "IAIM with the modified PPO algorithm significantly reduces the overhead by approximately 9.6% compared to MM with the standard PPO algorithm". The PPO baselines are ablations of the proposed IAIM with modified PPO; the static model (fixed RIS phases and routing, pp. 15-16) is non-learned, but no independent earlier learned method (e.g., DQN, DDPG) is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "We provide the complexity analysis for standard PPO and modified PPO algorithms in Table II". The order of complexity O[2((9N+9)l1+l1l2)+l2(N+1)+eps_t] is given for the modified PPO; Fig. 9c (p. 14) compares execution times of GA and GLAA.
q5_support: p. 12: "store this data along with simulated health parameters in the database". The data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and names no public dataset.
notes: Included under the jointly-learned clause of above_phy: the PPO action space contains the RIS phase matrix and transmit power together with offloading and CPU frequency (p. 11), and the abstract says PPO optimizes RIS configurations (p. 1). Most results concern MEC overhead and latency, so the reviewer should confirm this is not an above_phy exclusion. GLAA path selection is a non-learned heuristic and the RAG chat assistant is outside the physical layer. q3 is 0 because standard PPO and manual modeling are ablations of the proposed IAIM with modified PPO.
